title: The Power of Suggestion (Mind Field)
beats: Prestigious McGill study claims to read minds, but MRI machine is a sham; study is about faith in science
Placebo defined as something that shouldn't work but does; evolutionary hypothesis via child's pain signals
Placebos vary: doctor vs poker buddy, blue vs red, capsule vs injection, sham surgery
Meets three kids: Malaya (skin picking), Nicholas (migraines), Nathan (ADHD)
Fake non-functioning MRI as accessory-assisted placebo; scientists explain layers of deception
Neuroenchantment: cultural belief in neuroscience props gives them healing power
Ethics: kids told everything is suggestion; parents knew scanner was fake
Raise expectations via YouTubers; fake nurse, hallway, wait; scripted sound effects and suggestions
Original study: discarded hair dryer scanner convinced students it did many things
Adults put in fake mind-reading scanner: calibration, number guess, staged miss then sleight-of-hand hit
Reveal to the adult that machine is a speaker and deactivated; she calls it placebo
Dogs: 79% on placebo vs 86% on real seizure drug
Six-week results: Malaya's arms better, Nicholas no migraines, Nathan calmer and off medicine
No deception masked the placebo; placebo still works when subjects know
Closing: kids always had the power; all they needed was suggestion

metrics.misconception: partial: assumes placebo only works if you are fooled; refuted at 27:23
metrics.examples: 3 children over 6 weeks, then 1 adult demo, then dogs; case study not generalised mathematically
metrics.ending: Results from kids as payoff, ethics defence, placebo-works-when-known twist, summary line

principles.2: not-observed: no notation; terms like neuroenchantment introduced once
principles.5: confirmed: audience watches the experiment itself 8:45-21:14, even the adult mind-reading trick 15:38
principles.7: partly: viewer shares the adult's surprise at 19:05 before reveal at 21:14
principles.8: partly: steady speech; dwell in conversation scenes slows idea rate
principles.9: partly: three children's cases repeated through intake, session, outcome
principles.10: partly: child cases before adult demo, but not increasing difficulty
principles.11: partly: placebo definition, then variation, then kids, then adult demo
principles.12: confirmed: McGill Raz Lab, NC State dog study, original hair dryer study
principles.13: partly: plain language; justifies sham design via ethics quote at 8:13

new_moves.name: let-learner-be-fooled-then-reveal
new_moves.what: Put a real person through the illusion so viewers experience belief, then unmask the trick

new_moves.name: before-after-case-tracking
new_moves.what: Introduce subjects with symptoms, return with outcomes after elapsed time

new_moves.name: mechanism-by-staged-props
new_moves.what: Shows each deception layer (lab coat, nurse, waiting) so the mechanism is visible

theory: The video teaches that placebo works by making the audience first live inside the belief (the kids' sessions, the adult's mind-reading), delaying the explanation until the reveal. The reveal lands harder because the viewer felt the effect. It is persuasion-as-pedagogy rather than concept building.
velocity: Scene builder: roleplay simulation where learner experiences a fooled prediction and then gets the reveal
Orchestrator: delay the mechanism name until after a lived demo; add a 'reveal' beat
Learner model: elicit a guess before reveal, then compare to the true answer
Evals: check an honest-caveat beat (ethics, limits) exists whenever the lesson persuades
Ghost hands: show the props and steps of the deception one by one
quote: Studies show that even when subjects learn it was a placebo, results remain.
